niche_preference_profile: This user consistently prefers interfaces that feel complete, polished, and easy to scan, with enough content visible to feel useful but not so much that the screen feels crowded. They like clear sectioning, strong hierarchy, explicit labels, and obvious actions. Visually, they tend to favor light or airy themes, soft spacing, conventional settings-style layouts, and calm, reassuring presentation over dark, heavy, urgent, or placeholder-like designs. They also prefer concise copy, minimal clutter, and layouts that feel finished and intentional.

criteria.description: Prefers screens that feel fully populated, with multiple visible sections or rows and little empty space.
Prefers content to be evenly distributed vertically so the page does not feel top-heavy or bottom-empty.
Prefers clear section boundaries, labeled categories, and a strong hierarchy that makes the screen easy to parse.
Prefers a moderate-to-high amount of information on screen, enough to feel useful and complete without becoming chaotic.
Prefers interfaces that look intentional, app-like, and fully built rather than sparse, partial, or mockup-like.
Prefers each row or item to have a specific, descriptive label and an obvious purpose.
Prefers controls that clearly signal whether they are toggles, navigation rows, or direct actions.
Prefers familiar settings-list patterns such as full-width rows, light separators, and standard control placement.
Prefers light, airy backgrounds and softer visual treatment over dark, heavy surfaces.
Prefers short, direct, scannable copy over verbose or instructional text.
Prefers the main action to be immediately obvious and visually prominent.
Prefers friendly, reassuring, low-urgency messaging over harsh, alarmed, or overly urgent tone.
Prefers layouts with fewer competing elements, less chrome, and less visual noise.
Prefers related controls to be grouped together in a way that makes the screen easy to scan.
Prefers a single clear focal element, such as a hero image or main feature card, rather than many equally weighted modules.
Prefers generous but controlled spacing that creates breathing room without making the interface feel empty.
Prefers navigation and drill-in affordances to be easy to recognize and consistently applied.
Prefers the current status and next action to be clearly communicated in the interface.
